source_review.notes: Reviewed Princeton and Stanford trie materials, current Unicode Normalization and Text Segmentation annexes, the primary Adaptive Radix Tree paper, current Rust fst documentation, maintained Apache Lucene FST and libart implementations. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked alphabet Sigma, finite sequences, alphabet-unit length L, prefix relation, terminal membership, degree, key/node/total-symbol counts, canonicalization C, radix labels, and generations.
Checked bytes, Unicode code points, grapheme clusters, tokens, raw/display text, canonical keys, collation, logical keys, physical nodes, and output size remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every complexity statement identifies alphabet units and separates canonicalization, transition, comparison, and output costs.

evidence: Recomputed five canonical keys, decomposed acute update without size increase, four ca-prefix keys before deletion, and two car-prefix results.
Recomputed longest stored prefix cart for cartwheel, deletion of car preserving cart, final size four, and root children c,d.
Checked UTF-8 café uses five bytes versus four Unicode code points, while its decomposed form contains five code points before NFC.
Recomputed depth-five size-doubling illustration separately from trie costs and verified all ten worked examples' boundary counts.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable canonicalizer is explicitly fixture-bounded and is not empirical evidence of Unicode normalization conformance.

evidence: Verified exact lookup induction: after i unique transitions the node spells exactly canonical prefix k[0:i], with terminal required at L.
Verified insertion increments size only on nonterminal-to-terminal transition and update preserves size.
Verified deletion prunes exactly nonterminal childless suffix nodes and therefore preserves every other terminal path.
Verified radix sibling labels require distinct first symbols and splitting preserves concatenated root-to-terminal strings.
Verified prefix and fuzzy enumeration complexity must include traversal/state expansion and output.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Child lookup cost is conditional on fixed, sorted, hashed, bitmap, or adaptive representation.

evidence: Reviewed empty universe/key, prefix-versus-key, key with descendants, leaf/internal/absent deletion, duplicate update/reject, last child, and radix mismatches at every label position.
Reviewed composed/decomposed text, case expansion, non-BMP scalars, grapheme sequences, mixed scripts, bidi/confusables, invalid UTF-8, normalization expansion, and policy/version drift.

Reviewed hash flooding, huge prefixes/fanout/output, wildcard state explosion, stale counts/top-k, iterator invalidation, split/delete/read races, reclamation, offset overflow, cycles, unreachable nodes, and crash publication.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Resource limits cover raw bytes, canonical symbols, nodes, labels, degree, expansion, output, diagnostics, and reader-retained generations.

evidence: The executable DFS checks node identity is reached once, every child label is one code point in its finite model, nonterminals do not carry values, and terminal count equals size.
Operations exercise exact membership, update, prefix enumeration, longest prefix, deletion pruning, ordering, and root reachability.
The proposed independent full-key reference map avoids repeating the trie's prefix-node representation in tests.
invariant_checking.notes: The trace covers one mutable hash-child code-point trie, not compressed, adaptive, double-array, FST, persistent, or concurrent structures.

evidence: Reviewed sequence/alphabet and Unicode identity, uncompressed operations, pruning, prefix/longest lookup, child layouts, concrete memory, and ordering.
Reviewed radix splits/merges, Patricia/double-array/FST variants, subtree caches, wildcard/fuzzy bounds, iterator/handle generations, copy-on-write and lock-based concurrency.

Reviewed persistent logical/physical schemas, hostile parser validation, crash publication, security/resource controls, reference/exhaustive/metamorphic/fault/concurrency evidence, and representative benchmarks.
proof_review.notes: No Unicode identity or child representation is claimed universally appropriate.

evidence: Lookup induction, terminal membership, deletion pruning, and radix splitting are separated from empirical layout/performance claims.
Unicode standards define normalization and segmentation; the chapter explicitly separates case, collation, display, and security policy.
The executable labels its canonicalizer as one finite fixture rather than a general NFC implementation.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Maintained implementations are examples, not proof that the chapter's proposed API inherits their guarantees.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact thirteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded Python toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_trie_operations_trace and exercises five canonical keys plus one canonical-equivalent update and deletion.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No Unicode conformance suite, compressed/adaptive layout, fixed-width parser, concurrency, persistence, security, production memory, cache, ranking, or tail-latency workload was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed sequence identity first, then terminal/path invariants, operations, child layouts, compression/static alternatives, ordering/caches, lifecycle, persistence, security, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed versioned normalization/collation, display separation, byte/node/allocator accounting, duplicate/failure semantics, bounded autocomplete, rank-cache coherence, iterator generations, copy-on-write publication/reclamation, persistent offset validation, crash replacement, tenant authorization, and workload telemetry.

pedagogical_review.notes: Starts by asking what one key symbol means, derives exact/prefix/delete correctness, contrasts eight representation families, includes a bounded reproduced trace, ten examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/academic-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Unicode Consortium, Princeton, Stanford, ART, Rust fst, Apache Lucene, libart, security, localization, performance, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither general Unicode normalization/case/collation/security correctness, arbitrary alphabet/value policies, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, compressed/adaptive/double-array/FST correctness, iterator or handle stability, thread safety/linearizability, safe reclamation, durable persistence/crash recovery, hostile-parser security, production memory/cache/ranking/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
